question: A material with high toughness must have:
solution:
The correct answer is __high strength and high ductility.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Toughness__ is the ability of a material to absorb energy and deform plastically before fracturing.
 
• A material with high toughness must have both high strength and high ductility.
 
• High strength ensures the material can withstand large stress, while high ductility ensures the material can deform significantly without breaking.
 
• Examples of tough materials include steel and titanium alloys.
 
• It is a critical property for materials used in applications requiring resistance to impact and shock loads.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ductility:**

 
 
• Ductility is the ability of a material to deform plastically without fracturing.
 
• Materials with high ductility can be stretched into wires, such as copper and aluminum.
 
 
 
• **Strength:**
 
 
• Strength refers to the ability of a material to withstand an applied force without failing.
 
• Materials like carbon fiber and high-strength steels are examples of high-strength materials.
 
 
 
• **Impact Resistance:**
 
 
• Impact resistance is closely related to toughness and refers to a material's ability to resist sudden shocks or impacts.
 
• Materials with high toughness are often used in automotive and aerospace industries.
